Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this on. We are beginning a formal decommission of the EU-dedicated tenancy in Q2 and need to confirm exactly what artifacts Redwood will provide as evidence that all customer data for our tenant has been fully sanitized. Legal wants clear acceptance criteria so we can close our internal compliance ticket. High level asks: 

- Exact list of artifacts (logs, snapshot IDs, object deletion receipts, KMS key events) you can provide.
- Timeline expectations (how long after the scheduled decommission we can expect artifacts).
- Confirmation on whether backup replicas and cold snapshot archives are included in the wipe.
- A short attestation we can put into our audit record (signed by Redwood operator) stating data was destroyed per agreed process.

We have a legal hold on a small set of records; will that change the approach? Also please call out any third-party dependencies (cloud provider snapshot retention, tape archives) that we need to resolve before we can accept.

Appreciate a clear checklist we can review with Legal and Ops.

—Charlotte
Head of IT Security, FinSecure

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>

Charlotte — thanks for the clear list. Below is a proposed acceptance checklist from Redwood (we can iterate). I added short notes about where artifacts originate and estimated delivery windows. Attaching our sanitized checklist + sample scrub commands for engineering.

Proposed acceptance checklist (summary):
1) Tenant snapshot chain destruction
   - Artifacts: list of snapshot IDs for the tenant + deletion receipts (snapshot-delete events)
   - Where from: block storage snapshot service + Redwood control-plane event log
   - Delivery window: within 48 hours after final snapshot-purge job completes

2) Object store object deletion receipts
   - Artifacts: CSV of S3 object keys affected, object-delete event timestamps, and eventual 404 checks (where S3 returns NotFound)
   - Where from: object-store event logs and our scrub verification runner
   - Delivery window: 72 hours after job completion (object listing + verification)

3) Backup / cold-archive confirmation
   - Artifacts: list of any archival holdings, retention policy references, and deletion certificates if archived outside primary region
   - Note: for some cloud-provider deep-archive tiers there is a provider-side retention window that must lapse before irreversible destruction; we will surface those entries and recommended next steps

4) KMS key rotation and key state snapshot
   - Artifacts: KMS access log excerpt showing key-disable/rotate events and envelope-key metadata for the tenant (redacted where necessary)

5) Cluster evacuation and KV cache tombstoning
   - Artifacts: cluster drain logs, eviction timestamps, and KV cache purge receipts

6) Audit log extract and MD5/SHA256 baseline check
   - Artifacts: audit log extract covering the purge window, plus hash of final snapshot manifest for independent validation

7) Operator attestation
   - Artifact: brief signed statement from Redwood operations with date/time and list of artifacts delivered (PDF)

Clarifications and edge cases:
- Legal hold: If FinSecure has active legal holds for a subset of records, we will not execute destructive operations for those keys until we receive written release. We can provide isolated evidence for the remainder of the tenant.
- Cross-region replication: If tenant data was replicated out of the EU region (e.g., for DR) we will enumerate replicas and include them in the artifact list; destruction timelines may be gated by the remote provider's retention.
- Third-party tapes/archives: Redwood does not maintain tape media for hosted Dedicated deployments by default; if FinSecure requested offsite archival via a partner, we need explicit confirmation to remove those archives.

Next steps: please confirm: 1) desired decommission date window, 2) whether legal hold applies and to which dataset IDs, and 3) acceptance of the checklist above.

Deliverables attached: redwood-sanitization-checklist-v1.3.pdf, scrub-simulation-commands.txt (engineering samples).

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Manager, Trust & Safety — Redwood Inference

Adding operational detail (quick notes) — hi all.

Operational proofs we can produce today (sample snippets included):
- Snapshot delete receipts: control-plane event ID + timestamp. Example: EVENT 2027-03-09T02:10:34Z - snapshot-delete - snap-efs-ff12ac34
- Object verify run: our scrub runner will attempt HEAD on deleted keys and return 404; we produce a verification CSV with key, last-known-size, delete-time, and HEAD-result (404).
- Hashing: we can provide a manifest.json for the final pre-delete snapshot; we will compute SHA256 over the manifest and include the digest in the final package so FinSecure can validate the set of objects that were removed.
- KMS: we can show envelope key metadata and access logs; note we cannot share master-key material but will show key-state transitions (Disabled -> ScheduledDeletion) and Cloud KMS audit entries.

Small caveat re: provider cold-archive: some providers surface a 'restore window' after a delete where objects are recoverable for a limited interval; those entries will be flagged in the backup report. If FinSecure needs immediate irrevocable destruction for archived copies, we will coordinate escalation with the provider and estimate a provider SLA.

We can also run a one-off scrub simulation on a copy of FinSecure's tenant (no destructive ops) and provide the report so Legal can review expected artifact shape. Simulation can be scheduled in the next 5 business days.

Attaching a short script we use for verification and a redacted sample of the audit-log extract.

—Laura
Director, Platform Security, Redwood Inference

Attachment: scrub-simulation-commands.txt

- Please confirm whether any long-term cold archives were ever created for our tenant and, if so, the provider + retention window. If those exist we need timelines for irreversible deletion (or confirmation they were never created).
- We would like the scrub simulation report before the actual decommission so Legal can review the artifact format. Please book the simulation for next Wednesday (2027-03-17) if possible.

Once we have the simulation and the attestation template we will reconvene with Legal and confirm a decommission window.

—Charlotte
